chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sama'ani, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him: A man divorced his wife while he was ill, with a single divorce, and he had previously divorced her twice. He said: She inherits him if he is in his illness. I asked: What is the definition of the illness? He said: He remains ill until he dies, even if that lasts for a year.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of illness for inheritance purposes when a man divorces his wife?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the ruling of *talaq al-marid* (divorce of the ill), establishing that a single divorce pronounced during illness does not trigger the inheritance restriction typically applied to multiple divorces in that state. Shaykh al-Tusi records this view to define the threshold of 'illness' as a continuous condition persisting until death, distinguishing it from temporary ailments, thereby ensuring the wife retains her right to inherit the husband's estate.
